subject: Film & Cinema
title: The Rubber Hose Era
description: A quick win: understand The Rubber Hose Era.

hook.text: In the 1920s, cartoon characters had noodle arms and bendy legs. Everything was elastic.

buildup.text: The rubber hose style — named for its boneless limbs — defined early animation's look.

discovery.text: Felix the Cat and early Mickey Mouse used this style — simple, expressive, and easy to animate.

twist.text: The style died when Disney pushed for realism. Now it's back as a nostalgic aesthetic trend.

climax.text: Rubber hose animation reminds us that animation's greatest strength is impossibility.

punchline.text: Boneless characters had the most flexibility.

quiz.question: Why is it called 'rubber hose' animation?
options: Characters had boneless, rubbery limbs that bent freely
It was made with rubber stamps
